Investigation: Sky (Formerly MakerDAO) Peg Stability Module Processed $518M in Transactions Linked to Illicit Wallets, Including $101.9M Tied Directly to North Korean Hackers According to CoinDesk, an investigation by crypto risk analytics firm Inca Digital found that the Peg Stability Module (PSM) of Sky (formerly MakerDAO) has processed $518 million in transactions involving 422 wallets linked to illicit activities—including hacks, phishing attacks, and sanctioned entities—with $101.9 million directly tied to North Korean hackers. Within 10 days following the 2025 Bybit hack, associated wallets converted $91.5 million in assets through the PSM. Currently, Sky's PSM holds approximately $2.7 billion in USDC within a single Ethereum address; if Circle were to blacklist that address at the request of law enforcement, the entire reserve could be frozen, potentially impairing redemptions and the peg stability of DAI and USDS. In response, the Sky Frontier Foundation stated that the flagged transactions do not mean all funds were stolen assets, noting that the volume accounts for less than 0.06% of PSM's over $930 billion in cumulative volume and occurred almost entirely via third-party DEX aggregators rather than Sky's official website, which implements wallet screening. — link

Solana Unveils 2027 Roadmap, Doubling Compute Capacity and Cutting Unit Consumption by 80% Following the Alpenglow upgrade, Solana core development team Anza has outlined its 2027 technical roadmap for Solana across four pillars: Performance (doubling network compute capacity and cutting compute unit consumption by 80% for token account transactions); Expressivity (adding vector processing for models running fully onchain, raising the per-transaction account limit from 64 to 96, and reading account data directly rather than copying it to reduce data movement per transaction); Market Structure (building on Alpenglow with faster block distribution and introducing Constellation for clearer ordering rules and greater validator competition); and Resilience (simplifying the protocol with fewer special cases to make future changes safer). — link

October 2026 Exchange Website Traffic Report: MoM down 0.65%, OKX overtakes Binance for first place WuBlockchain data show that website traffic across nine major crypto exchanges totaled approximately 139 million visits in October 2026, down 0.65% month over month. OKX overtook Binance to rank first with 35.69 million visits (25.7% share), followed by Binance at 34.57 million (24.9%) and Coinbase at 22.14 million (15.9%). Bitfinex recorded the largest monthly increase (+10.9%), followed by OKX (+7.4%) and Bitget (+4.7%), while HTX (-22.5%), Upbit (-16.0%) and Bybit (-6.0%) saw the largest declines. The U.S. was the largest source of website traffic for OKX and Coinbase, while South Korea ranked first for Binance. — link
